proposed_statement_changes.reason: The former endpoint-proximity conclusion is not implied by outward constraint boxes: a retained box can meet the constraint interval without containing an exact-profile optimizer. The corrected claim keeps exact-profile coverage, requires a finite feasible witness in every decoder, controls every decoded law by the enlarged discrepancy threshold, and states the honest joint constraint/endpoint certificate count. This removes only the unsupported exact-endpoint transfer while retaining the operational coverage needed by the band theorem.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(\tau_n\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: Constraint feasibility must be enclosed at the squared-discrepancy scale independently of the endpoint-evaluation tolerance.

proposed_core_edits.name: \(\beta\)
proposed_core_edits.reason: The protected inverse and minimax width require only the one-dimensional Sobolev embedding threshold \(\beta>1/2\); the stronger threshold \(\beta>3/2\) is used only to simplify the endpoint-entropy contribution to the certificate count.

The original construction used one tolerance for logically different tasks and retained cells without a finite proof of decoder nonemptiness. The replacement separates \(\tau_n\) from \(\zeta_n\) and makes an explicitly encoded model-law witness part of every retained certificate.

The decoder must be nonempty for a finitely verifiable reason. The replacement uses the witness carried by each retained box and records the exact constraint enclosure needed to derive the enlarged-profile inclusion.

Endpoint optimization must exclude abstract or empty cells and must expose the interval radius used in the width proof. Every optimized cell now has a verified witness and every objective interval has radius at most \(\zeta_n\).

The established fixed-nuisance converse uses a weighted Jacobi reproducing-kernel packet and two fixed asymmetric mixtures of shifted and scaled sinc-fourth densities, not the obsolete Legendre/bump description.

proposed.justification: Operational honesty requires finite certificates for both continuum feasibility and nonempty decoded-law cells; width is then controlled on the enlarged certified profile.
proposed.gap: Finite-moment inversion does not by itself certify a continuum law profile, and a continuous discrepancy profile does not by itself provide checkable nonempty optimization cells.
proposed.consumer: Empirical users obtain reproducible endpoints with separately auditable constraint and endpoint tolerances; the statistical width absorbs profile enlargement through the protected inverse modulus.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem's claim, dependencies, and symbol closure must match the repaired witness-certified construction and the new constraint tolerance.

prose_updates.tldr: The observed law supplies an unmarked probability channel and an outcome-marked signed channel. Continuous integrated control on the moment-protected square, quantitative analytic continuation, and Sobolev recovery yield an honest simultaneous ADRF band with minimax expected maximal width \(r_n\asymp(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\) for every fixed \(\beta>1/2\). The operational algorithm uses the squared-discrepancy tolerance \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\) separately from endpoint tolerance \(\zeta_n\): every retained rational box carries a finitely checked model-law witness, the exact profile is covered by an enlarged decoded profile, and the protected inverse directly bounds that enlarged profile's diameter. A fixed-density Bernoulli marked experiment based on a weighted Jacobi packet and fixed asymmetric sinc-fourth-mixture errors supplies the matching lower bound.

project_justification.gap: Existing error-free ADRF work gives uniform inference, known-error methods give pointwise ADRF inference, and blind repeated-measurement work treats an unmarked density. None combines an honest whole-curve ADRF band, a sharp expected-width modulus, a finitely witness-certified continuum profile, and a fixed-nuisance marked converse when two replicate errors are unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric, and allowed spectral zeros.
project_justification.niche: Compact dose support makes both latent transforms entire, while the common error second-moment radius supplies a uniformly nonvanishing protected neighborhood. The inferential object is a paired nonlinear quotient. Feasibility is certified at squared-discrepancy scale \(\tau_n\), endpoint arithmetic at scale \(\zeta_n\), and statistical width is controlled from the diameter of the resulting enlarged law profile.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the paired protected inverse at exponent \(\beta-1/2\), embeds it in a continuously constrained confidence profile, covers that profile by finitely checkable boxes each carrying an explicit decoded-law witness, and derives endpoint width directly from the enlarged-profile inverse modulus. A Bernoulli marked weighted-Jacobi construction with fixed asymmetric sinc-fourth-mixture errors leaves the unmarked replicate law fixed and matches the upper rate.

prose_updates.related_work: Colangelo and Lee (2025), especially Supplementary Theorems S11 and S12, are the closest uniform-in-treatment ADRF comparator, but treatment is observed without error. Huang and Zhang (2023) derive pointwise ADRF inference with a known error transform. Gao, Bondell, Huang, and Gong (2024) estimate a latent-treatment ADRF through a variational neural model without a blind-replicate honest-band theorem. Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehericy (2025) provide the closest blind-replicate method exemplar through a continuous integrated analytic-polynomial contrast and compact-support density rates; the present lower experiment instead uses a weighted Jacobi reproducing-kernel packet in the Bernoulli marked channel together with two fixed nonidentical asymmetric mixtures of shifted and scaled sinc-fourth densities. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021) invert finite complex Kotlarski moment tests for an unmarked density but do not certify a continuum ADRF profile with nonempty decoded-law witnesses. Kato and Sasaki (2018, 2019) study density and errors-in-variables regression bands under auxiliary, symmetric, or conventional spectral information, while Neumann (2007) motivates integrated characteristic-function coordinates. Lounici and Nickl (2011), Genovese and Wasserman (2008), and Low (1997) inform sup-norm recovery and confidence-band lower reductions. These are informed-by comparisons; the separate error-free reduction is the only equivalence claim.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite certificate enlarges the exact discrepancy profile from \(\epsilon_n^2\) to \(\epsilon_n^2+2\tau_n\); its validity therefore depends on applying the protected inverse to the enlarged profile, not on any unsupported numerical proximity to exact-profile optimizers. Every retained cell must carry a finite model-law witness, and empty abstract decoders may not enter endpoint optimization. The width frontier holds for \(\beta>1/2\), but the endpoint entropy collapses into the simpler \(K_n^2\) coordinate term only when \(\beta>3/2\); the weak second-moment error class still contributes the separate worst-case term \(\tau_n^{-1/2}\log(C/\tau_n)\) to log certificate size. On the converse side, the weighted Jacobi packet must preserve Bernoulli range, Sobolev slack, fixed nuisances, and product-law affinity.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The frontier fixes \(\beta>1/2\), the support interval, Sobolev radii, overlap constants, outcome bound, and error second-moment radius. Error laws remain unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric, and may have zeros outside the protected neighborhood. The finite algorithm uses \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\) for constraint enclosures and \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\) for endpoint intervals; only the certificate-count simplification, not the statistical theorem, requires \(\beta>3/2\). Adaptation to unknown smoothness or drifting channel severity is outside the theorem. The error-free reduction remains a separate specialization.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The probability and signed marked channels are controlled by continuous integrated empirical contrasts on \(\mathcal C_*\). Entire-transform continuation and Sobolev recovery are profiled jointly. Constraint enclosures use \(\tau_n=\epsilon_n^2\), endpoint enclosures use \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\), and every retained finite box carries a checkable decoded-law witness.

statement_notes.justification: Operational honesty requires finite certificates for continuum feasibility and decoder nonemptiness, with constraint and endpoint tolerances audited separately.
statement_notes.gap: Prior finite-moment or continuous-metric methods do not establish exact-profile coverage by finitely witness-certified nonempty law cells together with a controlled enlarged-profile radius.
statement_notes.consumer: Users obtain reproducible endpoints whose numerical intervals are explicit, while statistical width is certified through the enlarged-profile inverse rather than an unproved optimizer-proximity claim.

statement_notes.justification: This is the constructive half of the simultaneous-band frontier and now controls width directly over the witness-certified enlarged profile.
statement_notes.gap: Existing ADRF and deconvolution bands do not handle blind asymmetric replicates with spectral zeros through a finite nonempty-law certificate.
statement_notes.consumer: Studies with two nonidentical replicate measurements can report a uniformly valid ADRF band with an auditable finite construction and worst-case width.

statement_notes.justification: The matching expected-maximal-width frontier is the theorem-level statistical contribution and holds throughout the Sobolev embedding range \(\beta>1/2\).
statement_notes.gap: No cited work matches a witness-certified honest ADRF sup-band upper bound to a fixed-nuisance marked lower bound under fully blind asymmetric replicates with spectral zeros.
statement_notes.consumer: Study designers can translate the frontier into sample-size calculations for resolving dose-response features.
